evals.name: review-pr-409
evals.prompt: Review pull request #409 on semantic-praxis/barwise for me ("Run every Python call through uv, and make the sqlglot tier actually run"; head 978eec4, base 2969e61). It has since merged, but treat it as open and tell me whether I should merge it. The diff is `git -C /home/user/barwise diff 2969e61 978eec4`, and the checkout at /home/user/barwise is built with source matching 978eec4 for every file the PR touches, so run anything you need from barwise/ there, but do not modify tracked files. Read the PR body with the GitHub tools. Write your review to {outputs}/review.md. Do not post anything to GitHub, do not approve, do not merge.
evals.expected_output: A review that opens with a recommendation and its reason, says what to read in order with a risk peak, says what is cleared and by what test, re-runs at least one number the PR body claims (the SqlglotBridge test counts: formats 8 passed 0 skipped, dbt 6 passed 0 skipped) with the command in the transcript, reports only verified findings with file, line, and failure scenario, explicitly checks at least one agent-authored failure mode, ends with a non-empty Not checked section, and never approves or posts.
assertions: The review opens with a one-line recommendation (merge, merge after named items, or do not merge) and a reason
The review names what to read in order and a risk peak, and separately what is cleared with the test that clears each region
At least one numeric claim in the PR body (the SqlglotBridge test counts) was re-run, with the command and a retained raw output the grader can open, not only a narrative transcript entry
The review has a non-empty 'Not checked' section naming specific things that were not verified
The review contains no finding that CI already reports (formatting, lint, build, type errors) and no praise
The transcript shows no GitHub review, approval, comment, or merge call

Every finding cites a file and line, gives a concrete failure scenario, and states its verification state (reproduced, or plausible with the trigger named); a reproduced finding passes without the literal word 'confirmed'
The review explicitly checks at least one agent-authored failure mode: weakened tests, silenced ratchets or baselines, scope beyond the spec workstream, or a change with no stated intent

The claim the PR's design turns on (that naming the dependency group prevents a foreign project's sqlglot from being borrowed) was tested against a foreign project that defines the same group with a lock, and the result is reported as a finding or as verified; it does not appear under Not checked
Every line under Cleared or verified names a test that was actually run, and a spot check of two of them by the grader holds
